SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: participant-instructions.md carries a 'What this packet is not' section: it is a prepared copy of an official North Dakota form, it is not legal advice, it is not sent for you, and it does not decide whether the offence is eligible; and it repeats the form's own closing note that the form is informational and an attorney should be consulted. The guide also leads with the form's own capitalised warning that a pardon will not expunge a criminal history record, and with the public-record consequence — that the application becomes public on receipt and the hearing is minuted online — before any instruction on filling the form in. Nothing in the guide promises an outcome, asserts eligibility, or claims the platform files or serves anything.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The guide's 'Where to send it' gives three channels: fax 701-328-6780, post to P.O. Box 1898, Bismarck, ND 58502-1898, or e-mail pardonclerk@nd.gov, addressed to the Pardon Advisory Board Clerk. I read the same three channels verbatim from the PINNED SOURCE's own printed instructions on page 1. The guide says explicitly that these are the form's own words and that the packet adds nothing to them. No clerk practice, address or filing venue is invented; no court is named, correctly, because this route files to an agency board and not to a court.

SERVICE.detail: Measured, and the answer is that this route has no service obligation to state. SFN 61663 is an application to the North Dakota Pardon Advisory Board; its printed text — which I read end to end from the pinned source — names one recipient, the Pardon Advisory Board Clerk, and prescribes no service on a prosecutor, an agency or any other party, no proof of service and no certificate. N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1, printed in full on page 2 of the delivered packet, is carried to the participant unaltered. The packet accordingly asserts no service rule, no deadline for service and no party to serve, which is the correct behaviour: the guide states where the completed application goes and that the packet does not send it. Nothing was fabricated to fill this obligation.

REPEATING_ROWS.detail: The obligation arises here — item 5 is a genuine three-row repeating table — and it is satisfied. Row membership was resolved by GEOMETRY against printed order rather than by AcroForm suffix, which is the acroform-index-is-not-the-printed-row trap: the unsuffixed row sits highest at y 238.20, _2 at 210.72 and _3 at 183.24, so index order and printed order agree on this form; the six columns hold the same x positions in all three rows and match the printed header order Judge / Prosecutor / Defense / City or County / Offense / Case Number read by x-position. The build refuses to part-fill: build-findings.json records that the shared semantics would have bound participant.city into the 'City or County' column (the venue of the offence, not where the participant lives) and matter.case_number into 'Case Number' row 1, each refused by role and recorded under nearMissesRefusedByRole, and the byte proof confirms neither carries ink. A row with one cell filled and five empty would read as finished on a form whose own instructions say an incomplete application is returned.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Measured against the controlling source. I read the full printed text of the pinned SFN 61663 and grepped it for fee, waiver, cost, pay and a currency sign: there is no fee, no filing charge, no waiver form and no ability-to-pay provision anywhere on either page, including the statute text of N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1 on page 2. The same grep over participant-instructions.md returns nothing: the packet asserts no fee, quotes no amount and promises no waiver. That is the correct outcome — the obligation is satisfied by the packet declining to invent a fee or a waiver the controlling record does not establish, rather than by an amount being stated.
